Theorem

↗ def:lorentz-metric ↗ prop:existence-riemannian-metric ↗ prop:lorentz-metric-of-rank-one-distribution ↗ prop:rank-one-distribution-of-lorentz-metric

1. ch2:2.69

A smooth manifold admits a Lorentz metric if and only if it admits a rank-1 tangent distribution, equivalently a rank-1 subbundle of $TM$.

Proof

↗ prop:lorentz-metric-of-rank-one-distribution ↗ prop:rank-one-distribution-of-lorentz-metric \sketch Apply Proposition 16 in one direction and Proposition 4 in the other.

□

Every noncompact connected smooth manifold admits a Lorentz metric, while a compact connected smooth manifold admits one if and only if its Euler characteristic is zero (see \cite{ON83}, p. 149). Thus no even-dimensional sphere admits a Lorentz metric. For further treatments of pseudo-Riemannian metrics, see \cite{ON83} and \cite{HE73}.
